title: perf-bench-scratch-amelia-ross-2026-03-20
content:
Quick scratchpad for today
Owner: Amelia Ross (notes to self)
Context:
- Goal: sanity-check latency vs throughput tradeoffs for MPT-like 13B on A100-80GB (dedicated pool) with and without KV-cache and different batch policies.
- Why: customer-facing latency SLOs target 150ms p95 for short completions (<=64 tokens). Need to see practical configs that meet that while keeping tokens/s cost reasonable.

Setup:
- Model: open-mpt-13B-raft (non-sharded run)
- HW: A100-80GB (NVIDIA), single-GPU per replica
- Runtime: latest local build (perf branch, kernel tweaks from PR #842)
- Quant: fp16 native runs, and an int8-ish experimental path (quant-profile q6) for a subset
- Batching policies tested:
  * none (single-request immediate)
  * fixed-batch-8 (collect up to 8 or timeout 10ms)
  * adaptive (auto-batch based on input length, target latency 120ms)
- KV-cache: on/off; warm cache = repeated prompt prefixes across requests
- Workload: 1-shot prompt template, avg input length ~28 tokens, output target 32 tokens

Runs and raw observations (p50/p95 latency in ms, throughput tokens/s):
1) Baseline (no batch, no kv-cache, fp16)\   - p50: 48ms, p95: 220ms, tokens/s: 120\   - Notes: p95 too high for SLO. Variability from cold KV init + scheduling jitter.
2) Fixed-batch-8, fp16, kv-cache off\   - p50: 65ms, p95: 140ms, tokens/s: 580\   - Notes: batching increases p50 but drops p95 dramatically. Good throughput.
3) Fixed-batch-8, fp16, kv-cache on (warm)\   - p50: 40ms, p95: 95ms, tokens/s: 810\   - Notes: warm cache reduces per-token compute and latency. p95 now comfortably under 150ms.
4) Adaptive batching, target latency 120ms, fp16, kv-cache on\   - p50: 45ms, p95: 110ms, tokens/s: 720\   - Notes: smoother tradeoff, slightly lower throughput than fixed-8 but better latency consistency.
5) Int8-ish (q6) fixed-batch-8, kv-cache on\   - p50: 38ms, p95: 88ms, tokens/s: 1200\   - Notes: big perf wins, but need to verify output quality (run eval). Potential for cost reduction. Watch for tokenization edge cases.
6) Stress run (ramp to 500 concurrent clients) adaptive, kv-cache on, fp16\   - observed system-level throttling at 460 clients -> increased queueing, p95 jumps to 320ms\   - tokens/s cluster-level: ~110k tokens/s before throttling

Quick micro-insights:
- KV-cache matters a lot for short, repeated-prefix workloads (e.g., chat turn flows). Warm cache -> 30-50% latency reduction and 40-70% throughput uplift depending on batch size.
- Fixed small batches (4-8) are sweet spot for p95 in single-GPU setups. Larger batches (>16) start to hurt latency SLO for short outputs.
- Adaptive batching is attractive for varied input lengths; configuration needs tightening to avoid high queueing under sudden ramp.
- Int8 path shows promise but we need a focused quality regression test set (JIRA PERF-291) prior to recommending for Dedicated customers.
- Under heavy concurrent load, cluster-level autoscaling/burst capacity needs exercise; saw throttling thresholds around ~460 clients for this config.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Run small A/B on output quality (BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity proxies + human spot-check) for int8 vs fp16 (assign Jordan).
- Add microbench with longer outputs (256 tokens) to see how KV-cache amortizes over longer generation.
- Verify behavior with multiple shards (2xGPU) \u2014 possible inter-GPU comm overhead increases p95.
- Check scheduler timeout tuning: fixed 10ms seemed OK, try 5ms to reduce p50 for interactive workloads (but might reduce throughput).
- Re-run stress tests with Dedicated burst-capacity policy enabled (talk to infra team: Sam Park).

Immediate next steps:
- Upload traces + perf flamegraphs to GH PR (redwood/serving-runtime#842) \u2014 I will attach logs from run 3 and 5.
- Create small eval harness for int8 quick-check (JIRA PERF-291) and schedule pair with Jordan this week.
- Draft short note for product on recommended defaults for Dedicated (suggest fixe-batch-8 + kv-cache warm)

Notes-to-self / random thoughts:
- Might be worth adding a short-circuit path in runtime for warm-cache small outputs to shave another ~8-15ms.
- Consider a per-customer default batching policy tuned by typical request length distribution (learned from telemetry).

Attachments referenced: perf-logs-2026-03-20.tar.gz (in Drive), perf-flame-run5.png (chart)

End of scratchpad.
summary: Bench scratch: A100 single-GPU MPT-like 13B; KV-cache dramatically reduces latency; fixed small batches (4-8) good for p95; int8 shows major throughput gains but needs quality checks. Next: int8 eval + stress runs with autoscaling.
